Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

divide verb

split into parts, share out

also divide up, split up, share out

classical

Caes. BG 1.1: Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs
Sen. Ep. 88.11: cum frātre dīvidere

dīvidō, dīvidere, dīvīsī, dīvīsum

verb, third conjugation

divide, split; share out

Into parts (in partēs) or among people (inter sē, cum aliquō); Seneca sets the surveyor’s division of a field beside sharing with a brother (Ep. 88.11).

Other words

  • partior, partīrī, partītus sum — share out, divide among

    also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.37 (Lewis & Short); Sall. J. 43.1, the active (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero and Caesar use the deponent; the active partiō is in Plautus and Sallust (Lewis & Short).

  • distribuō, distribuere, distribuī, distribūtum — distribute, share out

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.10 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rep. 2.22: populum in quīnque classēs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs

    Gaul as a whole is divided into three partsCaes. BG 1.1

  • Quid mihi prōdest scīre agellum in partēs dīvidere, sī nesciō cum frātre dīvidere?

    What use is it to me to know how to divide a plot of land into parts, if I don’t know how to share it with my brother?Sen. Ep. 88.11

See also divide, share, separate, part, cut.

SourcesLewis & Short: divido · Lewis & Short: partio · Lewis & Short: distribuo
